- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 2–5%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; apply downward correction of 3–8% to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model often undercorrects; add 1–3% upward bias to prevent premature bottoming.
- Model frequently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is neutral or mildly bullish; adjust downward by 1–4% for first 7 days.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish (or vice versa) within 3–5 days, model lags by 1–3 days; adjust forecast to align with sentiment shift 1–2 days ahead.
- Mean reversion is strong in 10–15 day horizon; if model holds price above 30-day moving average for >5 days, reduce forecast by 2–5% to align with reversion.
- If sentiment is high and price is near 30-day high, model often overestimates; cap forecast at 10–15% below recent high to avoid overbought bias.
